projects.name: BAMBO Finance Module
projects.role: Backend developer (Python/FastAPI) in a two-person team (backend + frontend)
projects.description: Cost-control and financial reporting module for BAMBO's construction-monitoring platform. It gives the owner one view of the original estimate, actual spend, current value of completed work and the budget needed to finish the project.

sections.title: Estimates, prices and invoices
items: Financial items in four groups (materials, labor, equipment and overhead) with an estimate per activity; the original estimate is never overwritten and every revision is recorded with full history.
Append-only price history, with prices entered manually, from Excel or from Google Sheets, and unit conversion.
Multi-line invoices with gap-free sequential numbering; a confirmed invoice cannot be edited or deleted and changes only through a correction or cancellation document.
Project progress read from Microsoft Project (MPP) files with the MPXJ library, as read-only snapshots.

sections.title: AI invoice capture
items: Invoice data extracted from photos with PaddleOCR and from Persian voice notes with Whisper; both run on the project's own server.
AI output is only a draft and has no effect on financial reports until a user confirms it.
Uploaded files checked in three steps (extension, file type and magic bytes); when extraction is unavailable, the system says so explicitly instead of guessing.

sections.title: Reporting and access
items: Management dashboard, report builder, print and PDF versions, and CSV/XLSX export.
Periodic reports stored as immutable snapshots; changes to current prices never alter earlier reports.
Each user can access only their own organization's and project's data, and invoice management needs a separate permission.

sections.title: Architecture and quality
items: 51 API endpoints on FastAPI and PostgreSQL 16, with separate domain, services and repository layers and parameterized SQL on psycopg (no ORM); the OpenAPI contract stays in sync with the code.
Financial integrity protected by 21 database invariants and a trigger that locks issued invoices; in a concurrency test, 6 simultaneous requests received 6 distinct numbers.
Safe migration on real data, verified by 30 acceptance tests over 53 existing invoices; issued numbers were preserved unchanged and downgrade was safe.
1,361 backend tests passing, with CI on GitHub Actions for every push.
Status: validated in an isolated environment; acceptance in the host's production environment is still pending.

projects.name: BAMBO Pilot Management Platform
projects.role: Backend developer (Python/FastAPI); backend and frontend were separate roles in this project
projects.description: A system that manages each BAMBO customer's pilot period before signing a contract: from project registration and drawing intake to field surveys, owner training, evaluation and the commercial offer.

sections.title: Workflow and approvals
items: The process is a state machine with 19 sequential stages and 5 approval gates (G1–G5); the next stage cannot start until the current one is approved.
Each stage has a checklist, submission, approval, rejection and correction; rejection requires a reason and errors are reported at the field level.
Five structured forms (F01–F05) matching the reference file: coordination, readiness, operations, customer success and incidents.
Each approval is saved as a hashed, immutable snapshot; later corrections create a new version and history is never lost.

sections.title: Login and access control
items: SMS one-time-password (OTP) login with rate limiting and a transactional lock.
Roles and an access matrix for every stage and gate, with access control switchable on or off by a single key.
SMS notifications with every attempt and delivery result logged, plus per-user notification settings.

sections.title: Field operations
items: Secure DWG drawing uploads checked for size, extension, MIME type and file signature; SHA-256 blocks duplicates and drawings are versioned.
Survey mission scheduling with time-overlap detection and PostgreSQL row locks, with a separate status for each floor.
Full incident lifecycle from report to closure, with response deadlines by severity (critical 30 minutes, major 4 hours, normal the same day); an open critical incident blocks gate G4.

sections.title: Reporting, architecture and quality
items: 9 key performance indicators (KPIs) such as successful upload rate, re-survey rate and average satisfaction; missing data is never reported as zero.
93 API endpoints and 24 Alembic migrations on FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2 and PostgreSQL; Persian PDFs with WeasyPrint and Jalali dates with persiantools.
Full audit of all 19 stages and 5 gates (UI, API, access, storage, notifications, approval and gate) with zero errors, and 218 pytest test functions.
Runs with Docker Compose, CI on GitHub Actions and runbooks for deployment, rollback and backup; a load test has not been run yet.

projects.name: ATK Online Accessory Store Backend
projects.role: Product owner and sole developer: from the requirements document (PRD) to architecture, implementation, tests and CI/CD
projects.description: A complete API for a direct-to-customer online accessory store, covering the whole purchase flow: catalog, cart, login, pricing, inventory, orders and online payment.

sections.title: Features
items: Product catalog with color, size and model variants, filtering and best-seller sorting.
Guest and user carts, merged after login; the final price is always calculated on the server.
Mobile-number OTP login, access and refresh tokens with rotation, and role and permission management.
Discount rules and codes with usage limits, address management, shipping methods and shipping cost calculation.

sections.title: Inventory, orders and payments
items: Temporary stock reservations that prevent overselling: tested with 20 concurrent buyers on a stock of 7 and 18 multi-item carts with crossed lock order, stock never went negative.
Checkout with an Idempotency-Key so a double click never creates a duplicate order; an order state machine and automatic cancellation when a reservation expires.
Payment results applied in a single transaction, late or duplicate payments moved to a "needs refund" state, and a reconciliation job for pending payments using an advisory lock.

sections.title: Architecture and quality
items: Modular monolith on FastAPI, fully async with PostgreSQL 16 through SQLAlchemy 2 and asyncpg; 66 API endpoints and 25 Alembic migrations.
About 927 tests in 77 files run in parallel, with code quality checked by strict mypy and ruff.
CI runs lint, type checks and tests, fails on skipped tests, scans for secrets with gitleaks and smoke-tests a staging environment; a Docker image is published to GHCR for each phase.

sections.title: Planning and status
items: The project is split into 6 phases and 148 tasks with clear acceptance criteria, with 52 architecture decision records (ADRs).
The MVP is fully implemented and about 66% of the whole project is done; the next steps are user accounts, the admin panel and release.

projects.name: Peak-Reversal Short Strategy: Backtesting on Gold & EUR/USD
projects.role: Data analyst in a four-person team at the Data Science Laboratory, Faculty of Mathematical Sciences (strategy design, backtesting and validation)
projects.description: A research project asking whether local price peaks on the 15-minute chart can be identified well enough to open short trades with a positive expected return. Teammates built a machine-learning version (Gradient Boosting); my part was a transparent, rule-based baseline plus the tests showing how far it can be trusted.

sections.title: Design and feature engineering
items: Built the full pipeline from raw OHLCV data to trade results.
Computed ATR(14) volatility and detected swing highs (a candle that is the highest within 3 candles on each side).

Designed an Exhaustion feature (upper wick ÷ ATR) that measures buyers failing to hold the high, and defined α* (the largest drop after a peak within the next 48 candles, normalized by ATR and capped at 5) as the measure of reversal strength.
Signal filter: confirmed peak, Exhaustion ≥ 0.6 and α* ≥ 1.0.

sections.title: Backtesting engine
items: Entry 0.7 ATR below the peak, stop-loss 1 ATR above and take-profit 1 ATR below the entry (1:1 risk/reward), with a 48-candle holding limit.
Results tracked in R-multiples and plotted as an equity curve, with breakdowns by period and by year.
Every distance expressed in ATR units, so the rules carry over without retuning between markets with very different prices (gold at about $2,000 vs EUR/USD at about 1.1).

sections.title: Results and robustness
items: Gold (2004–2025, about 488,000 candles): 12,878 simulated trades with a 72.2% win rate in the initial backtest.
Recent windows: 68.3% win rate over the last year, 71.7% over 6 months and 66.7% over 3 months (only 18 trades); no signals in the last month.
EUR/USD (2010–2016, 174,734 candles): yearly win rate between 71.9% and 77.4%, with 490–710 trades per year.

sections.title: Validation and limitations
items: Treating each peak as known only after its 3 confirming candles close (a realistic live-trading assumption), the gold win rate fell to about 48.5% over 11,469 trades: no edge before trading costs.

The α* filter barely changed the result (72.0% without it); almost all of the initial edge came from entering before the peak was confirmed, so the initial numbers are an upper bound, not live performance.
Next steps: confirmation-delayed entries, walk-forward testing, spread and commission costs, and replacing α* with a feature that only uses past data.

projects.name: Online Retail Analysis — Sales, Customers & Retention
projects.role: Data analyst; personal project from raw data to dashboard
projects.description: Analysis of over one million real transactions from a UK online giftware wholesaler (Dec 2009 – Dec 2011) to answer where sales growth came from, how dependent revenue is on a few customers and products, and how many new customers come back.

sections.title: Data and method
items: Public UCI Online Retail II dataset with 1,067,371 rows.
Data cleaning that set aside 3.8% of rows (40,355): duplicates, rows without a customer ID, zero prices and non-product codes; cancellations were analyzed separately.
Exploratory analysis in three notebooks, testable functions for KPIs, RFM, cohorts and LTV, and a 2-page Power BI dashboard.

sections.title: Key findings
items: Net revenue of £18.9M from 39,246 orders and 5,852 customers; the 2.3% revenue growth in the last year came from larger orders, not more orders.
High revenue concentration: 20% of customers generate 77% and 22% of products generate 80% of revenue; September to November makes up 41% of yearly revenue.
RFM segmentation identified 236 high-value customers at risk of churn, worth £901K.
About 21% of new customers buy again the next month; average customer lifetime value (LTV) is £634 at 3 months and £1,373 at 12 months.

sections.title: Quality and limitations
items: 117 automated pytest tests check the cleaning and calculations.
The data includes revenue only, not costs or profit; the LTV model is simple and based on past data.

projects.name: Maven Market Retail Intelligence
projects.role: BI developer; personal project from data model to dashboard and SQL queries
projects.description: Star-schema model and 6-page Power BI dashboard for a 24-store chain in the USA, Mexico and Canada (1997–1998), built to separate real sales growth from growth driven by new store openings.

sections.title: Data and model
items: 269,720 sales rows and 7,087 return rows for 10,281 customers, 1,560 products and 24 stores.
Preparation and quality checks in Python: duplicate rows flagged rather than deleted (to keep them traceable), 20 postal codes fixed and 57 days without sales identified.
Star schema with 2 fact tables (sales and returns) and 4 dimensions (date, customer, product and store).

sections.title: Implementation
items: Power BI report built as code (PBIP/TMDL) with 63 DAX measures; all 124 measure checks were correct.
Analytical and practice T-SQL queries run and validated on SQL Server, plus 173 automated tests.

sections.title: Key findings
items: Reported sales grew 112.2%, but same-store growth was only 8.4%, and 92.5% of the increase came from 11 new stores.
Gross margin stayed around 59.6% in both years and the return rate was 0.99%.
The top 10% of customers generate 39.9% of revenue; store size and sales have a correlation of -0.10, so bigger stores do not necessarily sell more.

projects.name: Did the Tehran Stock Exchange Beat Inflation?
projects.role: Data analyst; personal project covering data collection, ETL, analysis and dashboard
projects.description: A study of the Tehran Stock Exchange's real returns against the consumer price index over 36 months (2023–2026), asking whether investing in the market preserved purchasing power.

sections.title: Data and method
items: Daily prices of 8 major stocks, the overall, equal-weight and 7 sector indices from TSETMC, CPI from the Statistical Centre of Iran, and yields of 103 government bonds from Fara Bourse.
Python ETL in separate modules for fetching, quality control, preparation and analysis; TSETMC data errors, such as an index recorded at one-tenth of its value for 5 days, were found and fixed.
Real returns adjusted for inflation, 12-month rolling returns, stock correlations and a 4-page Power BI dashboard.

sections.title: Key findings
items: Prices rose ×3.62; the overall index lost 6.6% and the equal-weight index 26.4% in real terms, while cash rial lost 72% of its purchasing power.
Only 3 of 8 stocks beat inflation, and correlations of 0.70–0.95 between stocks limit diversification.
A 50-trading-day market closure caused a 15.6% real loss by reopening; government bonds also returned about -19% in real terms.

sections.title: Limitations
items: The sample covers 8 large stocks, not the whole market, over a three-year period; this analysis is not investment advice.

projects.name: TSE Market Monitor
projects.role: Data engineer and BI developer; personal project from ETL to data warehouse, scheduling, queries and dashboard
projects.description: A SQL Server data warehouse for all 747 Tehran Stock Exchange and Fara Bourse symbols: a repeatable, reliable foundation for daily market data rather than a one-off analysis.

sections.title: Data warehouse architecture
items: Separate staging, dw and etl layers; a star schema with 4 dimensions and 5 fact tables, where the symbol dimension is SCD Type 2 so renames and sector changes keep their history.
Incremental loads with stored procedures, MERGE and watermarks; loads are idempotent: the first run inserted 936,649 rows and a second run on the same data changed nothing.
Runs automatically Saturday to Wednesday at 16:00 with Windows Task Scheduler.

sections.title: Data quality and optimization
items: Reconciliation of total trade value between source and warehouse, with zero difference.
187 price-scale errors found and fixed, and 94 symbol first-listing days identified to avoid false returns.
One suitable index cut a query's logical reads from 11,464 to 64; 28 T-SQL queries were run and validated on the data.

sections.title: Dashboard and findings
items: 6-page Power BI dashboard with 43 DAX measures; all 112 numeric checks were correct, with 78 automated tests.
The overall index grew 304.5% in rials but fell about 23% in dollars.
Retail money inflow correlates 0.685 with same-day returns but only 0.283 with next-day returns: retail money follows the market rather than predicting it.
